designAnswers.inboxAppendAndHook: The inbox appends in appendCampaignCombatOutcomeBatch (campaignCombatOutcomeInbox.ts:68-143) inside the writer's appendWithExtension transaction (:80; SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:60-82). It can take U35e's rewrite as the SAME injected hook: the store's appendCombatOutcomeBatch (JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:467-484) passes this.rewriteRecordAfterCommand (installed by bindJournalCapabilityPorts, journalCapabilityPorts.ts:230-232, on the store the co-op host uses) as a new optional third argument, exactly as appendCommandBatch passes it (:443), and the inbox runs it on the extension's handle after the receipt insert in the committed arm (between :140 and :141). No second hook is needed: the outcome and a command both end in the same saved-record rewrite. That call site is in JournalCampaignEventStore.ts, the file flip.mjs flips; nothing inside src/lib/campaign reaches the inbox without it (the binder receives the store and the branch store, not the journal, journalCapabilityPorts.ts:63-66; the journal is a private field, JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:382). See flagFileTension.
designAnswers.rosterMapping: The saved record's roster is body.rosterProjection.units[] with readiness 'Ready' | 'Damaged' | 'Destroyed' (src/types/campaign/RosterUnitProjection.ts:112) and force membership body.forces[].unitIds; the checkpoint maps readiness to journal status Ready -> operational, Damaged -> damaged, Destroyed -> destroyed (campaignSourceGenesis.ts:51-55, :117) and rebuilds force membership from the forces, refusing a force that names an absent roster unit (:142-146). The rewrite (campaignRecordJournalState.ts:105-125) would set, for every unit present in both the journal roster and the projection, the projection readiness to the inverse of its journal status (operational -> Ready, damaged -> Damaged, destroyed -> Destroyed), and leave force unitIds unchanged: with a destroyed unit kept as a status change it stays in the journal and in its force, so projectForceUnits never meets an absent unit. A journal unit absent from the projection (a recoveredUnit; no unitRef, which projectRosterUnits refuses at :111-113) is not written (out of scope, FN-u35d-recovered-unit-lost); a record with an empty projection (placeholder units from forces, :95-101) has no readiness field to write. The host restores its roster store from the projection verbatim (useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts:520-547, on U35f's refresh :975), so the rewritten readiness reaches the host after the refresh (read, not run).
designAnswers.destroyedChangeKind: No new change kind is needed: the existing 'repaired' kind (the one the outcome already uses for a damaged unit) carrying unit.status 'destroyed' is a status change; the reducer upserts every kind but 'removed' (applyCampaignEvent.ts:47-56) and the schema pack accepts it (CampaignBaselineSchemaPack.ts:30, :77; measured p3: {change:'repaired', unit.status:'destroyed'} accepted; a new kind 'destroyed' refused by the change enum). So the schema pack is not the blocker. The blocker is where production derives the kind: CampaignMatchHostOutcomeInbox.ts:190 in src/lib/multiplayer/server (read-only for this lane). reconcileCoopBattle.ts:226, the line the sentence names, is reached only by the no-inbox walk (:131 routes every inbox-capable store to host.commitCombatOutcomeConsequences), and production always builds an inbox-capable store (getCampaignEventStore.ts:116-124, :131-134). Measured: with :226 edited as the sentence says, the production inbox path still commits 'removed' for the destroyed unit and the journal drops it (p1 unchanged); only the in-memory fallback keeps it as destroyed (p2).
designAnswers.duplicateReceipt: The inbox reads its receipt row by outcome id inside the append's immediate transaction before appending (campaignCombatOutcomeInbox.ts:81-101): the same version answers 'duplicate', a different version 'outcome-version-conflict', both without appending. Running the rewrite only in the committed arm after the receipt insert (:117-141) makes it run once per outcome id. The outcome command id campaign-outcome:<campaign>:<match>:<version> (CampaignMatchHostOutcomeInbox.ts:98) commits in the same transaction as the receipt row, so the writer's recorded-command answer (SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:176-183) is reached only with a receipt row present, which the lookup answers first; mirroring U35e's recorded-command check (JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:310-319) as well would cost one query. The host maps a duplicate to ok with no events (CampaignMatchHostOutcomeInbox.ts:102; reconcileCoopBattle.ts:133-134), and the server also records the battle per entry before the walk (bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:783-794). Measured on the baseline (p4): the second receipt of the same outcome answers ok with 0 events, the journal gains no event and the record version stays 1.
designAnswers.stalePutAfterOutcome: With the rewrite, the outcome's transaction advances the saved record's version (version + 1), so a whole-campaign PUT at the pre-outcome version fails the CAS (CampaignPersistenceService.ts:186-187) and the route answers 409 {kind: 'conflict', reason: 'base-state-unavailable', currentVersion, current: the rewritten record} with nothing appended ([id].ts:228-255), as after a command since U35e. The host browser takes the new version through U35f's refresh when it folds the outcome's CampaignEvent frames, which the host publishes after the commit (CampaignMatchHostOutcomeInbox.ts:120). So row o2u (a save built before the fold) would answer 409 instead of losing the debit. INFERENCE from the code: not measured, because the unit stopped at admission. Today (measured p1, p4) the outcome leaves the record at version 1.

blocker.whyNotInsidePaths: Production reconciles every co-op battle through the inbox path (reconcileCoopBattle.ts:131-145 -> CampaignMatchHost.ts:299-317 -> CampaignMatchHostOutcomeInbox.ts:67-122), whose event derivation is at :134-200. The host appends, applies and publishes the same derived events (:95-121), so changing them anywhere downstream inside src/lib/campaign (the store or the inbox) would make the journal disagree with the host and its broadcast. A record-only patch that re-adds a removed unit as Destroyed would keep the journal's removal, which the owner's decision replaces with a status change.

risksForTheParent: Authority: on a journal-native campaign every first-receipt combat outcome would write the saved record (version + 1, the journal's balance, date and roster readiness), so a host save built before the outcome answers 409 with the server record; the host adopts the new version through U35f's refresh on the outcome's frames (read, not run).

Idempotency: the rewrite belongs in the inbox's committed arm only; a duplicate or an outcome-version conflict answers before append() (campaignCombatOutcomeInbox.ts:81-101) and must rewrite nothing (measured today: a second receipt appends nothing, p4).
Concurrency: the rewrite must run on the extension's handle inside the outcome's immediate transaction, so a whole-campaign PUT is ordered wholly before or after the outcome.

Migration: none under OD-mvp-hard-cutover; like U35e the rewrite would spread the raw stored JSON without the read migration ladder. The owner's Lane B ruling is required on the head that merges (authority, idempotency, concurrency, migration).

Visible change: a destroyed unit is no longer deleted from the journal. It stays in the host state and every mirror with status 'destroyed': the guest's roster count counts it (CampaignCoopRouteSurfaceConnected.tsx:373-375), the activity feed reads '<designation> repaired' under 'technical' for it, as it already does for a damaged unit (campaignActivityProjection.ts:165-172), and any consumer that treats rosterUnits as the units still in service sees it (read, not run).

Documented invariant: rosterProjection readiness is documented as always equal to deriveRosterReadiness(campaign.unitCombatStates[unitId]) (src/types/campaign/RosterUnitProjection.ts:107-112); a rewrite that patches readiness from the journal without unitCombatStates makes that comment untrue for the saved record (read, not run).

findingsReportedNotFixed.finding: The destroyed -> 'removed' mapping that production commits is at CampaignMatchHostOutcomeInbox.ts:190, not at reconcileCoopBattle.ts:226, which only the no-inbox walk reaches; measured p1/p2 with :226 edited.
The outcome inbox can take the rewrite hook only from the store's appendCombatOutcomeBatch, in the flag file the charter's final check asks byte-identical (U35e F4 precedent).
Patching rosterProjection readiness from the journal leaves unitCombatStates as stored, so the documented readiness invariant would not hold for a rewritten record.

With the existing 'repaired' kind a destroyed unit's activity line reads '<designation> repaired' (category technical), as a damaged unit's does today; a new change kind would be refused by the schema pack (measured p3) and needs src/lib/events/replay and src/types/campaign/CampaignSync.ts, both outside the path.
